pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/110541

There's an unwritten invariant in ES|QL that's worth spelling out: a command's/logical plan's output attributes need to have unique names. In contrast to SQL, there's no way to disambiguate in cases like

```
ROW a = 1, a = 2 | eval b = 2*a
```

because we do not have qualifiers, like `some_table.a`. Instead, ES|QL performs variable shadowing, like in `EVAL`, where the rightmost assignment wins:

```
| EVAL x = 2*some_field, y = -some_other_field, x = x + y
```

`EVAL`'s output will have the attributes `y` and `x` - the rightmost one.

Let's enforce this invariant in our dependency checker; there's only one deviation from it, currently, which is `ROW` - I think this is a bug which this PR also fixes.

This is only enforced for logical plans; the dependency checker for physical plans is yet to be enabled as part of https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/105436.

Depends on https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/110793
pr_title: ESQL: Validate unique plan attribute names
pr_comment: Hi @alex-spies, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
Hi @alex-spies, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.

> Regarding `row` yes it seems there is an inconsistency between it and the rest of the commands. But first, let's make sure we cover all the commands from the point of view of attribute names uniqueness and if all stands then we can change `row`:
> 
> * `rename a as foo, b as foo` keeps the last `foo`

All other commands respect unique output attribute names. Behaviorally, only `GROK` and `RENAME` stand out:
- `GROK` doesn't self-shadow; if there's 2 times the same attribute name in the pattern, like `%{WORD:foo} %{WORD:foo}`, it will create multivalues. This is consistent with the Grok ingest processor, so we want to keep it this way.
- `RENAME` renames in place, it doesn't place the renamed columns at the right hand side. For usability, I think it's important it stays this way.

> * look into `enrich`, `grok`, `dissect`, `mv_expand` regarding names uniqueness

All good here, thanks for pointing this out - let's cover all our bases!

> * see if any wildcarded names (where they are allowed - `keep`, `drop` maybe some other places) don't trip the unique names verification

Done! I was afraid about wildcards in `RENAME`, but we correctly disallow them (`VerificationException`).

> * combine this change with [whatever needs to change in union types](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/110490) so that the whole story makes sense project-wide

Sounds good, I'll look into it!

> * look into fields and sub-fields where the name have dots - `rootfield.subfield.subsubfield` - we usually don't test these and that's a pity

Added a new test index to our csv tests with such a hierarchical mapping, and added tests using them to all commands that are relevant IMO.

I also confirmed that we treat hierarchical fields like this like plain fields - the `name` just becomes `rootfield.subfield.subsubfield`. Qualifiers are not used. On that note, also `FieldAttribute.path` and `FieldAttribute.parent` seem unused.

> Try also to push `mv_expand` to its edges.

Hmm, `mv_expand` takes only a single field name (resp. single attribute in the corresponding Java class); one can't even provide a list of field names due to parsing exceptions. I'm not sure which edge cases could create non unique attribute names; did you have something specific in mind?

> > Try also to push `mv_expand` to its edges.
> 
> Hmm, `mv_expand` takes only a single field name (resp. single attribute in the corresponding Java class); one can't even provide a list of field names due to parsing exceptions. I'm not sure which edge cases could create non unique attribute names; did you have something specific in mind?

Nothing concrete, but mv_expand has a different/special way of defining the output (aka "expanded" attribute) by creating a mirrored attribute of the "target" one.

> > > Try also to push `mv_expand` to its edges.
> > 
> > 
> > Hmm, `mv_expand` takes only a single field name (resp. single attribute in the corresponding Java class); one can't even provide a list of field names due to parsing exceptions. I'm not sure which edge cases could create non unique attribute names; did you have something specific in mind?
> 
> Nothing concrete, but mv_expand has a different/special way of defining the output (aka "expanded" attribute) by creating a mirrored attribute of the "target" one.

I took a look; the way we're using it right now, `MvExpand` is nice and consistent.
During [resolution](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bfc32a2acc8942dea31c7ac1f893805906b833fb/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/analysis/Analyzer.java#L493-L507), we hand it a new reference attribute (not referring to anything, similar hack to enrich) with the same name.

When computing the [output](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bfc32a2acc8942dea31c7ac1f893805906b833fb/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/plan/logical/MvExpand.java#L34-L38), we replace the initial, multi-valued attribute by this new reference attribute with the same name.

This is not failing the unique name validation added in this PR, so I think we should be good.

The way I can see MV_EXPAND compute inconsistent output, is only if the child plan before `MV_EXPAND` is already inconsistent (multiple attributes with the name of the expanded attr), or we misuse `MV_EXPAND` by giving it a differently named `expanded` field (currently doesn't happen in the LogicalPlanBuilder), or an optimization is buggy.
Okay, this will continue failing CI until https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/110793 is merged, but otherwise should be ready.

Thanks for your reviews, @leemthompo , @astefan , @craigtaverner and @luigidellaquila !

I updated `keep.asciidoc` one more time (I noticed the info I added would be duplicated), then it's time for a merge!

review_comment:
Actually, I changed my mind on this:

It is the actual name that needs to be unique; otherwise, bugs could slip in because we somehow end up using qualifiers on accident; qualifiers are not respected by our optimization rules, e.g. `mergeOutputAttributes`;  this [PR](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/110581) demonstrates that qualifiers are entirely unused, and the validation for the current state should reflect current assumptions.

If we end up using qualifiers after all (I think that's really for the future and we should really remove them until then), we can easily update the validation.
Not sure I understand why p should be resolved, while p.children should be unresolved. Should it not be `p -> p.resolved() == false || p.childrenResolved() == false ? p : doRule(p)`

This was carried over from `AnalyzerRule` and `BaseAnalyzerRule` while collapsing their execution logic into this simple `Rule`.

Currently it says "I'll just return the current plan without changes (i.e. skip) if it's either already resolved or has yet-to-be resolved children". I think this is correct.
